Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity title-screen direction concept for AI FRONTIER, an original browser RPG.
Primary request: Make a remarkable complete Game Boy Advance inspired 16-bit pixel RPG title screen. It must feel like a commercially art-directed game invitation. A young field trainer and three original AI companions look across a sunny river valley toward a richly detailed village and distant relay observatory. The companions are a coral owl scholar with a glowing feather, a jade fox scout with an origami golden tail, and a small cobalt twin-headed salamander with starlit fins.
Composition: wide landscape 16:9 screenshot, no browser chrome or device mockup. Large beautifully hand-pixelled AI FRONTIER logo in upper center over open blue sky; landscape depth layers, river reflections, wind in trees, footpath leading toward village. Trainer and companions in foreground occupy lower right, three-quarter backs with readable silhouettes. Compact pixel menu on lower left with a clear selection arrow.
Exact on-screen text: "AI FRONTIER", "Begin Journey", "Continue", "Practice", "Settings". No other copy.
Palette: full daylight GBA palette, clear cerulean sky, deep jade foliage, terracotta rooftops, ochre paths, warm sun, dark plum outlines, restrained coral accents. The world carries the color. Bright and inviting, tactile pixel clusters, convincing material detail, expressive creatures. Hand-placed hard-edged pixels, coherent low-resolution pixel scale; absolutely no anti-aliased vector look, blurry painting, 3D plastic, generic web cards, neon navy dashboard, glass panels, dense explanatory paragraphs, corporate logos or existing game characters. This is a concept for review, not an asset atlas.

Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: alternate high-fidelity title-screen direction concept for AI FRONTIER, an original browser RPG.
Primary request: A Game Boy Advance inspired pixel RPG title screen built as a living top-down village diorama. Highly finished hand-pixelled 16-bit art, meaningful small details, cozy character and readable game UI. This direction should compose the page very differently from a panoramic cinematic poster.
Composition: wide landscape 16:9 screenshot, no browser or console bezel. Most of the screen is a beautiful top-down starting town wrapped around a sunlit circular plaza, canal, stone bridge, red-roofed companion guild, gardens, animated-looking market flags and a great brass relay tree. A small trainer with a coral scholar owl follows a winding path through the scene. Other original companions are a jade origami-tailed fox and a cobalt twin-headed salamander near the guild. On the RIGHT quarter, a tall integrated off-white pixel menu panel with a small pixel logo and generous selectable lines; clear arrow next to primary action, decorative compass stamp rather than web icons. The scene is inviting and legible.
Exact text only: "AI FRONTIER", "Begin Journey", "Continue", "Practice", "Settings".
Palette: saturated leaf green and turquoise water cover most of the scene, ochre stone, vermilion roofs, warm early afternoon highlights, plum-blue shadows. Crisp pixel clusters and selective dithering, evocative of 2000s handheld RPG craft. Avoid generic website hero layout, SaaS cards, neon black-and-gold, overly dark blue shell, blurry pseudo-pixels, 3D rendering, corporate logos or existing game characters. This is a direction probe, not a shipped interface.

Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: standalone full-body companion avatar concept for an original GBA-inspired browser RPG, AI Frontier.
Image 1 is a STYLE REFERENCE for the world and creature art family only.
Style: excellent expressive 16-bit handheld RPG pixel art, shaped pixel clusters, a consistent dark-plum one-pixel outline at a logical 96x96 art scale, limited 12-16 color character palette, three-step pixel shading, crisp nearest-neighbor enlarged edges. Appealing character silhouette visible at thumbnail size, specific crafted details, three-quarter front view facing slightly left. One character only, full body including tail/feet, generous clean margin, centered, no crop, no lettering, no logo, no frame, no environment or platform, no glow haze. Genuinely transparent alpha background. This is a redesign concept/avatar; do not create an animation sheet.
Emberquill: an original coral-and-copper owl companion, thoughtful and brave. Big amber eyes, asymmetric long brow feather like a quill, strong rounded chest, layered wing feathers that resemble a folded scholar's mantle, plum collar with a tiny brass clasp, one small luminous golden feather held at the wingtip. Talons visible. Intelligent face, charming confident attitude; richer anatomy and distinctive silhouette.

Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: playable OVERWORLD screenshot concept, 16:9 landscape, for original GBA-inspired browser creature RPG AI Frontier.
Image 1 supplies the approved detailed town art family, not camera perspective or menu layout. Draw a true orthographic top-down handheld RPG play view (roof tops and small front building walls, north-up square tiles), NOT isometric diorama perspective.
Primary request: Frontier Crossing, a carefully authored river village with terracotta-roofed Companion Guild, small healing garden, market awning, a stone canal bridge and a striking brass relay tree landmark. Deep jade tree masses, bright grass edges, ochre paths, clear turquoise water with hard pixel reflections. A small human trainer in coral travel cap/jacket and backpack is on the path near the bridge; a coral owl companion follows one step behind. Both use a coherent 24x32-style field sprite scale, the trainer is tiny relative to the town, not a giant portrait. Distinct small NPC field sprites, readable walking paths, one signpost and a tempting side route. The scene should feel like a real tilemap viewed through a 480x270 logical camera.
UI is minimal: a modest location plaque in upper left with exact text "Frontier Crossing", three tiny companion party portraits in upper right, a small "Menu" label, and one local interaction prompt near the guild sign reading "Read sign". World occupies almost all the viewport. No bottom dashboard paragraph, no huge map name stamped across terrain, no website navigation, no giant buttons.
Style: precise 16-bit GBA pixels with consistent tile scale, tight color ramps, clear collision silhouettes, layered canopy and roof depth, warm and richly observed but readable. No painterly blur, low-poly 3D, neon dark shell, browser bezel, flat square-room placeholder map or existing game assets. This is a visual target for the planned tilemap, not a claim it is implemented.

Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity full battle-screen concept, 16:9 landscape, for original GBA-inspired creature RPG AI Frontier.
Input image 1 is the character identity for Emberquill. Image 2 is a world-art and palette reference, not a layout to copy.
Primary request: Beautiful readable classic handheld turn-based battle screen with a dedicated sunlit forest-river battlefield. Draw Emberquill's large BACK/three-quarter-back battle sprite near left foreground facing the far opponent. Preserve coral feathers, asymmetric quill brow, plum scholar mantle and gold feather. On far RIGHT, an original Static Wisp faces the player: a compact violet static cloud creature with pale mothlike fins and a small amber shard core, expressive eyes, no menacing horror. The environment has layered jade trees, grass, ochre stones, a ribbon of turquoise water and no distracting clutter over the sprites.
Battle UI: upper LEFT compact light pixel HUD reading "STATIC WISP  Lv 4", "HP 24/24", with a green HP bar. Lower RIGHT just above the command strip, compact light pixel HUD reading "EMBERQUILL  Lv 5", "HP 28/32", "EN 3/6", plus three small party markers. Bottom 25 percent is a confidently structured light pixel command area: left two-thirds reads "What will Emberquill do?" and the right third has exactly four menu commands in a 2x2 block: "Fight", "Team", "Pack", "Retreat", selection arrow at Fight. One coherent double-line plum pixel border, generous text size, crisp pixel font. No extra words.
Style: crafted GBA 16-bit pixel clusters, clean readable battle silhouettes and planned negative space, warm daylight colors and plum ink. Actual game screenshot composition, no browser/console chrome, no floating web cards, no neon blue shell, no blur, no 3D rendering, no existing game characters or logos. This is a UI direction concept and must clearly show the battle choreography/layout, not a character lineup.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Image 1 is the edit target, an original AI Frontier battle concept.
Change ONLY the three small red-and-white spherical party icons in the player HUD next to "Lv 5". Replace them with three ORIGINAL square companion seals: a coral square with a simple gold feather, a jade square with a simple pale leaf, and a cobalt square with a simple cyan droplet. Keep them tiny and clean at the existing scale, with dark plum pixel outlines and no circle/capsule design. Preserve the exact entire battle composition, all text and numbers, HUD frames, backgrounds, creature identities and pixel artwork unchanged. No other alterations. The three seals must not resemble any existing game's balls or logos.

Asset type: standalone full-body TRAINER avatar concept, original AI Frontier GBA-style RPG.
Image 1 is a style and wardrobe-color reference, and shows the original trainer from behind. Create the corresponding original front three-quarter trainer portrait in the same expressive pixel family.
Subject: an approachable young adult field explorer with medium brown skin, short dark wavy hair under a plain clay-red travel cap, coral short travel jacket, cream shirt, dark charcoal rolled hiking trousers, sturdy brown boots, compact tan backpack with a brass compass buckle and a tiny attached field notebook. A pale jade neck scarf and small brass field instrument hanging from the belt. Relaxed ready-to-travel stance, one hand holding backpack strap, friendly curious brown eyes. Independent original design, no badges or marks from any existing franchise.
Style: charming crafted 16-bit handheld RPG pixel portrait, clean dark-plum outline and three-step shading, shaped hard pixel clusters; full body and backpack visible, centered single figure, generous clear margin. Match the companions' warm expressive craft. Genuinely transparent background, no text, logos, scene, floor shadow, frame, pedestal, device or sprite sheet. This is an appearance concept for the player trainer, not an animation atlas.

Use case: background-extraction
Image 1 is the edit target. Make the original AI Frontier trainer a clean full-body transparent avatar.
Remove ONLY the background, including every brown/dark smoky glow or halo around the figure and below the boots, to genuinely transparent alpha. Preserve the trainer's exact identity, face, pose, clothing, backpack, accessories, pixel-art edges and colours. Keep all hair, straps and boot details. Do not add a ground shadow, pedestal or gradient, do not redesign or crop the trainer. Transparent pixels should begin immediately outside the character silhouette with no lingering glow.
